name: Arlington Park Special Purpose District
source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 465 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 465.

PD 465.

Arlington Park Special Purpose District

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 465 was established by Ordinance No. 23049, passed by the Dallas City Council on February 26, 1997. Ordinance No. 23049 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Ordinance No. 23049 was amended by Ordinance No. 25494, passed by the Dallas City Council on February 11, 2004. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 23049; 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 465 is established on property generally bounded by Record Crossing Road, Lee Hall Street, the C.R.I. & P. Railroad, and Stemmons Freeway (Interstate Highway 35). The size of PD 465 is approximately 154.54 acres. (Ord. Nos. 23049; 26042)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) For purposes of determining the applicability of regulations in this article and in Chapter 51A triggered by adjacency or proximity to another zoning district, this district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. For purposes of interpreting the DIR and RAR requirements of Division 51A-4.800, Area 3 is considered to be a single family residential zoning district, Areas 2, 6, and 7 are considered to be multifamily residential zoning districts, and Areas 1, 4, 5, and 5A are considered to be nonresidential zoning districts.

(d) In this article, SPECIAL RESIDENTIAL USE means a residential facility containing shared kitchen and laundry facilities that provides temporary housing and food to individuals and families who have children under the age of 19 that are receiving treatment at area hospitals, and may include residential facilities for housekeepers or resident managers. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042; 26145)

sections.title: Creation Of Subdistricts
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.104. CREATION OF SUBDISTRICTS.

A map labelled Exhibit 465A shows the boundaries of the district and eight areas. Property descriptions of the areas are attached as Exhibit A to Ordinance No. 25494, as amended by Section 1 of Ordinance No. 26145. In the event of a conflict between Exhibit A of Ordinance No. 25494, as amended by Section 1 of Ordinance No. 26145, and Exhibit 465A, Exhibit A attached to Ordinance No. 25494, as amended by Section 1 of Ordinance No. 26145, controls. (Ord. Nos. 23049; 25494; 26042; 26145)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

The provisions of Section 51A-4.702, “Planned Development (PD) District Regulations,” relating to the PD preapplication conference, site plan procedure, site analysis, conceptual plan, development plan, development schedule, and amendments to the development plan do not apply to this district, except that development and use of Area 7 as a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 465B). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the development plan, the provisions of this article control. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this district:

-- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations contained in Division 51A-4.400. In the event of a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard.

(1) Area 1. Minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(2) Area 2. Minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(3) Area 3. Minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(4) Area 4. Minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(5) Area 5. Minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(6) Area 5A. For a special residential use, minimum front yard on Lee Hall Drive is 50 feet and minimum front yard on Chattanooga Place is 15 feet. For all other uses, minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(6) Areas 6 and 7. Minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) Area 1. Minimum side and rear yard is:

(A) 20 feet when adjacent to or directly across an alley from a single family or duplex use; and

(B) no minimum in all other cases.

(2) Area 2. Minimum side and rear yard is five feet.

(3) Area 3. Minimum side and rear yard is five feet.

(4) Area 4. Minimum side and rear yard is:

(A) 20 feet when adjacent to or directly across an alley from a single family or duplex use; and

(B) no minimum in all other cases.

(5) Area 5. Minimum side and rear yard is:

(A) 20 feet when adjacent to or directly across an alley from a single family or duplex use; and

(B) no minimum in all other cases.

(6) Area 5A. For a special residential use, minimum side yard along Lee Hall Drive is eight feet and minimum side yard along Chattanooga Place is 34 feet. For all other uses, minimum side yard is 20 feet when adjacent to or directly across an alley from a single family or duplex use and no minimum in all other cases. Minimum rear yard is 20 feet when adjacent to or directly across an alley from a single family or duplex use and no minimum in all other cases.

(7) Areas 6 and 7. Minimum side and rear yard is five feet.

(c) Density.

(1) Area 1. Maximum dwelling unit density is 50 units per acre.

(2) Area 2. Maximum dwelling unit density is 12 units per acre.

(3) Area 3. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(4) Area 4. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(5) Area 5. Maximum dwelling unit density is 15 units per acre.

(6) Area 5A. For a special residential use, maximum number of beds is 16. For all other uses, maximum dwelling unit density is 15 units per acre.

(7) Areas 6 and 7. Maximum dwelling unit density is 12 units per acre.

(d) Floor area ratio.

(1) Area 1. Maximum floor area ratio for all uses is 1.8:1.

(2) Area 2. Maximum floor area ratio is 0.5:1.

(3) Area 3. Maximum floor area ratio is 0.5:1.

(4) Area 4. Maximum floor area ratio is 2.0:1.

(5) Area 5. Maximum floor area ratio is 2.0:1.

(6) Area 5A. For a special residential use, maximum floor area ratio is 0.33:1. For all other uses, maximum floor area ratio is 2.0:1.

(7) Areas 6 and 7. Maximum floor area ratio is 0.5:1.

(e) Height.

(1) Area 1. Maximum structure height is 70 feet.

(2) Area 2. Maximum structure height is 30 feet.

(3) Area 3. Maximum structure height is 30 feet.

(4) Area 4. Maximum structure height is 60 feet.

(5) Area 5. Maximum structure height is 70 feet.

(6) Area 5A. For a special residential use, maximum structure height is 24 feet. For all other uses, maximum structure height is 70 feet.

(7) Areas 6 and 7. Maximum structure height is 30 feet.

(f) Lot coverage.

(1) Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph, maximum lot coverage is:

(A) 45 percent for residential structures; and

(B) 60 percent for nonresidential structures.

(2) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(3) Maximum lot coverage for a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school in Area 7 is 35 percent.

(4) Maximum lot coverage for a special residential use is 33 percent.

(g) Lot size.

(1) Area 1. No minimum lot size.

(2) Area 2. Minimum lot area per dwelling unit is:

(A) 5,000 square feet for single family structures;

(B) 5,000 square feet for duplex structures; and

(C) no minimum in all other cases.

(3) Area 3. Minimum lot area per dwelling unit is:

(A) 5,000 square feet for single family structures;

(B) 5,000 square feet for duplex structures; and

(C) no minimum in all other cases.

(4) Area 4. No minimum lot size.

(5) Area 5 and 5A. Minimum lot area per dwelling unit is:

(A) 5,000 square feet for single family structures;

(B) 5,000 square feet for duplex structures; and

(C) no minimum in all other cases.

(6) Areas 6 and 7. Minimum lot area per dwelling unit is:

(A) 5,000 square feet for single family structures;

(B) 5,000 square feet for duplex structures; and

(C) no minimum in all other cases.

(h) Stories.

(1) Area 1. Maximum number of stories is five.

(2) Area 2. Maximum number of stories is two.

(3) Area 3. Maximum number of stories is two.

(4) Area 4. Maximum number of stories is five.

(5) Area 5. Maximum number of stories is five.

(6) Area 5A. For a special residential use, maximum number of stories is two. For all other uses, maximum number of stories is five.

(7) Areas 6 and 7. Maximum number of stories is two. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042; 26145)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations (Division 51A-4.200) for the specific off-street parking requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations (Divisions 51A-4.300 et seq) for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally.

(b) Off-street parking for a public school other than an open-enrollment charter school in Area 7 is permitted in the required yards.

(c) For a special residential use, a minimum of 0.3 parking spaces must be provided for each bed. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042; 26145)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Tree Preservation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.111. TREE PRESERVATION.

The regulations contained in Division 51A-10.130, “Tree Preservation,” apply to this PD. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided below, all landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article
X.

(b) For all nonresidential uses, all off-street surface parking areas, excluding driveways used for ingress or egress, must be screened from the street by using one or more of the following two methods to separately or collectively attain a minimum height of three feet above the parking surface:

(1) Earthen berm planted with turf grass or ground cover recommended for local area use by the director of park and recreation. The berm may not have a slope that exceeds one foot of height for each two feet of width.

(2) Evergreen plant materials recommended for local area use by the director of park and recreation. The plant materials must be located in a bed that is at least three feet wide with a minimum soil depth of 24 inches. Initial plantings must be capable of obtaining a solid appearance within three years. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.113. SIGNS.

(a) Areas 1, 4, and 5. Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts contained in Article VII.

(b) Areas 2, 3, 5A, 6, and 7. Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042; 26145)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Paving
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.115. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 25494; 26042)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-465.117. ZONING MAP.

PD 465 is located on Zoning Map Nos. I-5 and I-6. (Ord. Nos. 23049; 26042)
